checks: Apply the depth-root result to [0,1]×K with base dimension one and take any fixed base slice. Its raw ordinary depth on that slice is δ_K. The roof is nonnegative, bounded, concave and upper semicontinuous; thus its hypograph is compact and convex. An interior ball gives a uniform positive cap-volume lower bound over a smaller ball, so the lifted body has interior.

At an original boundary point a supporting hyperplane exists for the compact convex body. Its outward containing halfspace captures only the face in that hyperplane, of zero d-volume. Nonnegativity forces depth zero there. The graph image is exactly the rim and lies on the lifted boundary because r≥0.

The homothetic image about an interior point with factor 1−ε lies in int K by the interior-ball convex combination. Hence the volume of ∂K is at most [1−(1−ε)^d]|K| and is zero as ε decreases to zero. The isometric rim copy in the d-plane at height zero has zero H_d measure. The pushforward is concentrated there and is therefore singular.

For d=1 the roof is the tent of the nearer endpoint distance, its hypograph is a triangle, and its two rim points are vertices of zero H_1 measure. The proof applies independently to every interval of the example.

summary: The graph sends every original boundary point to height zero. The resulting closed rim has zero ambient d-dimensional surface measure, so every nonzero finite positive original boundary measure pushes forward singularly.
